# Snapshot 001 vs Snapshot 002 — Dimension-by-Dimension Comparison

Per Prompt 17 §21, using the dimensions Prompt 14 established. No single overall score. Every verdict below cites concrete evidence from `reconstruction_002.json`, the real source document, or `devils_advocate_review_001.md`.

## SOURCE IDENTITY FIDELITY — **IMPROVED**
Snapshot 001 packed `document_id`/`revision`/`issue_date`/`issuer`/`status` into an ad hoc `Source.note` string (`"document_id=NREOCRC-OPR-001; revision=0; ..."`) — functional but unqueryable, and flagged by its own report as a gap. Snapshot 002 populates real first-class `Source` fields (Batch F), derived generically from the machine-extracted front-matter table (a Field→attribute keyword mapping, not typed from memory). One field regressed to explicitly-unset rather than guessed: `issue_date` ("December 8, 2026" is free text, not ISO-8601 — left `NOT_EXTRACTED` rather than parsed with an ad hoc guess). Net: structured, queryable identity now exists; one sub-field honestly deferred rather than silently dropped.

## REQUIREMENT FIDELITY — **IMPROVED**
Snapshot 001: 18 hand-paraphrased requirements, not persisted as real objects (Requirement didn't exist) — held only in a report file. Adversarial Review 001 §2 found two concrete paraphrase losses: 12.1 dropped "at design-basis ambient conditions"; 2.2 compressed a two-part conjunctive test into "(bounded)". Snapshot 002: 59 real Batch F `Requirement` records; `text_reference` for the 56 bracket-derived ones is captured **verbatim by regex**, not paraphrased — both previously-lost qualifiers are now present in full, structurally, because nothing summarized them. Nuance: this verbatim-capture guarantee applies only where the source carries its own bracket tag; the 2 unlabeled clauses (2.2, 8.1) still required a human to transcribe (done verbatim this time, but classification left `None` rather than invented).

## AUTHORITY FIDELITY — **IMPROVED**
Snapshot 001 invented non-canonical authority strings for 3 unlabeled clauses (2.2 "STATED HIERARCHY (provisional)", 8.1 "STATED (general)", 12.2 "INFORMATIONAL (labelled...)") — flagged by Adversarial Review 001 §1 as ad hoc. Snapshot 002's 56 generically-derived requirements use **only** the document's own literal bracket labels (mandatory/rated/indicative/informational — zero `reference` instances exist in the source, confirmed absent, not missed). The 2 still-unlabeled clauses are left `classification=None` — more honest than inventing a label, at the cost of solving fewer clauses automatically. 12.2 (the specific weak point Adversarial Review 001 flagged — an INFORMATIONAL label collapsing a bylaw-derived minimum with an assumed estimate) is not registered as a Requirement at all in Snapshot 002 (it's a table, no bracket tag) — the over-generalization risk is avoided, but at the cost of 12.2 having zero representation (see Under-Interpretation Audit).

## SOURCE-LOCATION TRACEABILITY — **IMPROVED**
Every Snapshot 002 requirement carries a real `source_location` (clause/table_row + identifier). The real Batch F `validate_requirement_location_citation()` function was run against the two highest-value citations Adversarial Review 001 scrutinized: 12.3's claimed reference (VALID — "4.5" literally present, "4.3" literally absent, directly reversing Snapshot 001's mis-citation) and Row 20's claimed Section-14 reference (VALID). Snapshot 001 had no such mechanical check available at all (Requirement/citation-validation didn't exist).

## TABLE SEMANTICS — **IMPROVED (substantially)**
Snapshot 001: zero table structure; rows were "meaningless raw-pipe fragments" per its own gap log. Snapshot 002: 5 real tables extracted with headers+rows (Batch H). The Functional Program table was mechanically reconciled by a generic (group/qty/unit-value/subtotal, keyword-identified) algorithm — independently reproducing, to the exact figure, every mismatch Adversarial Review 001 computed by hand: 615≠570, 534≠850, 731≠1120, 175=175, 545=545, 410≠460, 195≠260; line-item/subtotal-cell/grand-total totals of 3,205 / 3,980 / 4,105 m². No number here was hard-coded — the reconciliation function has no NREOCRC-specific values in it.

## GRAPHIC TRACEABILITY — **PARTIALLY IMPROVED / bounded ceiling unchanged**
Both snapshots register the two SVGs as Sources with real hash/dimensions. Snapshot 002 additionally extracts each SVG's own embedded `<text>` labels generically, textually confirming "RESTRICTED COMMUNICATIONS SUB-ZONE" (as 3 literal text nodes) appears in Figure OPR-2.1. Neither snapshot has, or claims, any visual/spatial/geometric interpretation of the diagrams — that ceiling is untouched by Batch H (no vision capability exists), and this experiment does not pretend otherwise.

## CROSS-MODAL RELATIONSHIP COVERAGE — **IMPROVED**
Snapshot 001: 7 hand-picked relationships. Snapshot 002: 11, all produced by one generic regex mechanism (Section/Figure mention scanning over each requirement's own text) applied uniformly — not selected per-clause by a human. This directly fixes the 12.3→4.3 mis-targeting Adversarial Review 001 §3 called "a concrete, correctable error" (now 12.3→4.5). Real remaining gap: bare container-level references ("Section 14", "Section 18") and multi-target range references ("Sections 12.1 through 12.3" — only "12.1" is captured) are not resolved to specific targets; correctly left unresolved rather than fabricated.

## TEMPORAL / FUTURE-INFO ACCURACY — **UNCHANGED (re-confirmed, not re-tested by new mechanism)**
Both snapshots agree: no date exists anywhere in the document beyond the Issue Date; the Proposal Submission Deadline is referenced repeatedly but never dated. No `TemporalObligation` was created in either run — correctly, since no date exists to found one on.

## EXPECTED-INFORMATION ACCURACY — **IMPROVED, with one new self-inflicted false-confidence finding**
The clearest win: Snapshot 001 completely omitted NREOCRC-RFP-001 (status: "Issued concurrently") from its Expected Information Profile — Adversarial Review 001 §5 called this "arguably the single most important document-level gap in the whole review." Snapshot 002 builds its profile from a **generic loop over every row** of the Section 3 cross-reference table (found generically, not hand-picked), so RFP-001 is automatically included, correctly bucketed apart from the four genuinely-"to be issued" documents. The omission cannot recur because the mechanism no longer hand-selects rows. However: (a) the underlying evaluator gap — no `SUFFICIENCY_*` outcome for "explicitly deferred, undated" — is **still open**, unaddressed by Batches F/G/H; the same human-layer-override workaround Snapshot 001 needed is still needed. (b) A **new** minor false-confidence artifact was found in this run's own matching logic: the Functional Program row's raw evaluator output reads `expected_not_found` despite the document being present, because this script's observed-evidence matcher only compared against the exact string `"NREOCRC-OPR-001"` and the Functional Program's own row reads `"Appendix OPR-1 (this document)"`. This is a bug in the lab script's matching heuristic, not in production code — but it is a real, freshly-introduced inconsistency, reported here rather than smoothed over.

## FALSE POSITIVES — **not qualitatively worse; risk surface grew with volume**
No confirmed false positive in the actual content produced. Self-audit specifically checked the five named failure patterns (Prompt 17 §23) — none occurred: not every clause became a Requirement (56/58 registered required an explicit bracket tag; ~40+ other numbered sub-sections were not registered), not every numeric difference became a Finding (exactly one, from real cross-checked computation), not every "see Section" became a strong dependency (unresolved references were left unresolved, not forced), the table mismatch was not called non-compliance, and figure references were not treated as spatial evidence. One structural risk flagged: the row-boundary detector (flag rows whose Security Level contains "/") is a generic heuristic that could over-trigger on a differently-structured document; it happened to fire exactly once, correctly, here.

## FALSE CONFIDENCE — **one new instance found; one pre-existing instance unchanged**
New: the Functional Program expected-information mismatch above. Unchanged: the raw `expected_not_found` output for the four genuinely-deferred documents still risks being misread as "missing/deficient" by anyone consuming that field without the accompanying human-layer bucket label — the same risk Snapshot 001 had, because the evaluator itself was not touched.

## UNRESOLVED-AMBIGUITY PRESERVATION — **IMPROVED, with a scanning-coverage caveat**
Because bracket-derived `text_reference` values are captured verbatim, hedge language survives by construction, not by a human remembering to preserve it — confirmed for 11 sections via a generic keyword scan (4.2, 2.2, 5.3, 6.1, 14.3, 15.1, 16.1, 18.1, 19.3, 20.1, 20.2). Caveat: the scan's own keyword list is not exhaustive — it did **not** flag 9.4 ("to be described in the Data Room"), Row 8 ("per Data Room"), or 13.3's full phrasing, all of which Adversarial Review 001 §9 found by full manual re-read. Importantly, the underlying `text_reference` for 9.4/13.3 *does* still contain those hedges verbatim (a human reading the record directly would see them) — only this run's automated *scan* under-reported them, which is a narrower miss than Snapshot 001's paraphrase actually *deleting* the qualifier.

## MISSED RELATIONSHIPS — **IMPROVED, not exhaustive**
Row 20 (Adversarial Review 001's single strongest "missed requirement" finding) is now captured via two independent generic mechanisms (slash-in-Security-Level + narrative Row-N backreference) that converge correctly, with zero manual prompting for "row 20" specifically. Sections 8.3, 5.4, and 18.2 — all three specifically named as missed in Adversarial Review 001 §1 — are now captured automatically (all three carry bracket tags the generic rule reads). Remaining, honestly-reported misses: 12.2 (no representation at all — a table without a bracket tag), the multi-target range-reference case, and the precedence list (Section 2.2) which is captured as an ordered text list but not wired into the Relationship graph (no Source exists for "Addenda"/"the Project Agreement" to point at — an honest absence, not a fabricated edge).

## FINDING QUALITY — **IMPROVED (qualitative, not just quantitative)**
Snapshot 001: zero Findings — the single point Adversarial Review 001's Overall Assessment called "wrong." Snapshot 002: exactly one real Finding, produced by an actual `AnalysisRun` (not fabricated to match a known answer), stating precisely the reconciliation problem Adversarial Review 001 identified by hand. Kept deliberately provisional — no Disposition, no non-compliance claim — with a `ReviewThread` routing Attention to the **Owner**, not the Design-Builder, matching Prompt 17 §9's explicit steer that this is an inconsistency in an Owner-issued document.

---

**Summary shape of the change:** every dimension that depended on *generic structural extraction actually existing* (table semantics, source identity, cross-references, expected-information completeness, finding quality) improved, several of them by fixing the exact specific defects Adversarial Review 001 named. Every dimension that depends on *domain reasoning no batch added* (the undated-deferral evaluator outcome, the design/procurement maturity-axis conflation, natural-language date parsing, unlabeled-clause default classification) is honestly unchanged. One new, minor, self-inflicted false-confidence artifact was found and is reported, not hidden.
